$comment: Story 6.8, FR-58, AD-2. Tracked upstream contribution register: gaps in the wrapped bmad-loop engine, Marshal's own compensating workaround, and upstream status. Hand-curated -- git review decides content changes (mirrors the CFE-side cwe-seed-gap/spdx-schema-gap suggesters' own 'the curated map stays hand-owned' precedent). Content transcribed from the PRD's own FR-58 section (prds/prd-pyforge-marshal-2026-07-25/prd.md, section 7.9 and its cited cross-references), not invented. Read by 'marshal upstream'.

entries.gap: bmad-loop has no built-in detection of a session that has stopped producing output but has not exited (a wedged interactive prompt, a stalled turn) -- the only prior stopgap was an external tmux + log-mtime watchdog.
entries.workaround: core/supervise.py's idle-detection ladder (AD-9/AD-20): a supervisor process, outside the harness session, samples externally-observed liveness (wall clock, process liveness, output modification time) and never trusts session self-report.

entries.gap: bmad-loop supports only run-level model selection -- one configured adapter model applies uniformly across every story in a sprint; a per-story model key is an upstream request (PRD 7.7).
entries.workaround: core/spec_difficulty.py's declared-difficulty parsing plus cli/spin.py's model_tier_map policy composition (Story 6.1, FR-48/FR-51/AD-19): Marshal resolves each story's declared difficulty and writes the tiered model choice into the rendered policy.toml bmad-loop itself reads, batching per-launch rather than per-story where the harness cannot honor a finer grain.

entries.gap: _bmad/bmm/config.yaml hard-codes planning_artifacts: "{project-root}/_bmad-output/planning-artifacts", and that key does NOT compose with a project's own output_folder override -- every BMAD write-skill resolves through one shared symlink pair per working tree, never a per-project path directly.
entries.workaround: cli/init.py's own marker+symlink convergence machinery: each loop home carries its own active-project marker and planning-artifact symlinks, independent of every other home and the main checkout (FR-2), with agreement checked and a desync reported rather than silently tolerated.

entries.gap: No Agent Communication Protocol (ACP) evaluation exists in bmad-loop for a versioned, neutrally-governed cross-agent adapter contract -- every adapter integration today is a bespoke CLI-probe/subprocess wrapper against the harness's own declarative profiles.
entries.workaround: adapters/harness_bmadloop.py's single wrap-not-absorb seam (AD-2/AD-3) plus the harness's own six declarative adapter profiles as the interim adapter contract, backstopped by the probe/conformance-smoke/matrix machinery (Epic 6) as a substitute portability proof until ACP migration trigger Q-6 fires.

entries.gap: bmad-loop's multiplexer backend detection had no declared non-POSIX (Windows-native) backend -- multiplexer_backend_available always reported unavailable off POSIX, a hard constraint for Windows-native operators without WSL.
entries.workaround: cli/init.py's own MRS-PREFLIGHT-003 preflight check surfaced the gap explicitly (never silently degraded) while it was open -- no functional workaround beyond honest detection existed prior to the upstream fix.
entries.note: Landed upstream 2026-08-01: bmad-loop v0.9.0 shipped a Windows psmux multiplexer backend. Entry closes as delivered -- the MRS-PREFLIGHT-003 workaround is flagged for review/removal now that a real backend exists.

entries.gap: bmad-loop's dev pass self-marks its story `done` in the sprint feed BEFORE review converges. When the review then fails and the story is deferred, nothing rolls the feed back -- a false green in the artifact the dashboard renders and the next run dispatches from, so the board over-reports AND the next run skips a story that was never finished. Caught 3 live on 2026-07-31 (marshal 1-6, doctor 1-4, mason 1-3), all the same shape: dev completed, review failed.
entries.workaround: scripts/story_status_check.py -- a repo detector that audits every `done` feed entry against a merge commit or a harness-recorded commit_sha (AD-33: git owns repository facts) and reports only when the harness positively says deferred/escalated. Containment, not a fix: the feed stays wrong, the detector just refuses to let it pass silently.
entries.compensating_fr: n/a -- repo detector, not a Marshal FR

entries.gap: When bmad-loop spends its damping cap it files 'follow-up review still recommended' into implementation-artifacts/deferred-work.md -- gitignored Tier-3, invisible to CI and absent from every clone -- under a generic DW-<n> id that the next damped story collides with. Measured 2026-08-09: DW-1/DW-2 were promoted by hand as DW-FU-1-1/DW-FU-1-3; DW-3..DW-7 never were, and stand as five tier3-only-deferral findings.
entries.workaround: scripts/deferred_work_check.py reports the tier3-only entries; promotion into planning-artifacts/deferred-work-ledger.md under the DW-<story>-<n> convention is manual. Marshal FR-175 makes the promotion an obligation of the story rather than later archaeology.

entries.gap: bmad-loop writes governed code with no knowledge of the repo's spec-surface contract, so every loop-produced story that touches governed files reds scripts/spec_surface_check.py until a human names the changed paths in the owning Spec's .memlog.md. Measured 2026-08-09 on the first three loop stories ever landed (doctor 6.2-6.4): 14 governed paths across spec-pyforge-doctor, plus pixi.toml against two further surfaces, all named by hand at landing.
entries.workaround: Manual per-file naming at landing, under the S-13.2 rule. Marshal FR-174 makes the loop do it as part of the story; the loop is deliberately never handed --write-baseline, since a producer that can stamp its own baseline is the laundering that rule exists to end.

entries.gap: bmad-loop's scm.max_parallel knob exists but is inert: policy.py:448-451 names Phase 5 parallel fan-out "not built yet," and policy.py:815-817,841-842 clamp any requested value to 1 unconditionally in loads(), with no diagnostic surfaced to the caller. Marshal's own rendered .bmad-loop/policy.toml carries the identical hardcoded max_parallel = 1 (adapters/harness_bmadloop.py:320) with no explanation either.
entries.workaround: core/policy.py's max_parallel seed key (Story 3.13, FR-184) lets a project's requested value compose and be recorded rather than tripping the generic unknown-key finding; MRS-POLICY-007 (Verdict.WARN) fires whenever the resolved value exceeds 1, naming the value and bmad_loop 0.9.0's own unbuilt Phase 5 scheduler as cause. The rendered policy.toml still writes the harness's own stock max_parallel = 1 -- that remains the only truthful effective value until the upstream scheduler ships.
